enonce.texte:
Read the following email and identify each component: Subject Line, Greeting, Body (Purpose, Details, Action), Closing, and Signature.

Subject: Request for Code Review on Authentication Module

Dear Team,

I hope this email finds you well. I have completed the implementation of the OAuth 2.0 authentication module for the user service. I would appreciate it if you could review the pull request and provide feedback by Wednesday.

The PR is available here: [link to PR]. Please let me know if you have any questions.

Best regards,
John Doe
Software Engineer
images: A screenshot of an email interface with labels pointing to Subject, Greeting, Body, Closing, and Signature sections.

questions.texte: Identify and name the different components of the professional email.
questions.reponse: Subject Line: 'Request for Code Review on Authentication Module', Greeting: 'Dear Team,', Body: 'I hope this email finds you well... let me know if you have any questions.', Closing: 'Best regards,', Signature: 'John Doe, Software Engineer'.

sousQuestions.texte: Analyze the purpose of each component. Why is it important to have a clear subject line?
sousQuestions.reponse: A clear subject line helps the recipient quickly understand the email's purpose. It allows them to prioritize their inbox and respond appropriately. Without a clear subject, the email might be overlooked or delayed.

enonce.texte:
For each scenario, identify the appropriate tone and formality level for the email.

  • Scenario 1: Writing to your manager to request a day off
  • Scenario 2: Writing to a colleague to ask for help with a bug
  • Scenario 3: Writing to a client about a project delay
  • Scenario 4: Writing to a recruiter about a job application
images: A diagram showing a spectrum from 'Informal' to 'Formal' with different communication situations.

questions.texte: Classify each scenario by its appropriate tone: Formal, Semi-formal, or Informal.
questions.reponse: Scenario 1: Semi-formal, Scenario 2: Informal, Scenario 3: Formal, Scenario 4: Formal.

sousQuestions.texte: Compare the language you would use in Scenario 2 vs. Scenario 3. Give specific examples.
sousQuestions.reponse: Scenario 2 (colleague): 'Hey Sarah, could you take a look at this bug when you have a moment? I'm stuck.' Scenario 3 (client): 'Dear Mr. Johnson, I am writing to inform you that we have encountered an unexpected technical issue. We are working diligently to resolve it and will provide an update by tomorrow morning. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience.'

enonce.texte: You are a software engineer working on a team project. The project is behind schedule because a key dependency is not working. Write a professional email to your team lead explaining the situation, requesting support, and suggesting a solution.
images: An illustration of a person typing on a laptop, looking concerned, with a calendar showing a deadline approaching.

questions.texte: Write the email. Include all necessary components: subject line, greeting, body, closing, and signature.
questions.reponse: Example answer: 'Subject: Urgent: Blocked by Authentication Service Dependency. Dear [Team Lead], I hope you're having a good week. I'm currently blocked on the user dashboard implementation because the authentication service dependency is returning errors. The service is not accepting JWT tokens, which is preventing any API calls from working. I've tried debugging locally and checking the service logs, but I haven't found the root cause. Could you please help me escalate this to the DevOps team? Or perhaps we could schedule a quick sync to review the issue together. In the meantime, I can work on the frontend UI components that don't require the API. Let me know your availability. Best regards, [Your Name]'

sousQuestions.texte: Evaluate the effectiveness of your email. Does it clearly communicate the problem, the impact, and the requested action?
sousQuestions.reponse: The email clearly communicates the problem (authentication service errors), its impact (blocked on implementation), and the requested action (help with escalation or a sync meeting). It also suggests a temporary solution (working on other tasks). It is professional, concise, and respectful.

enonce.texte: You sent a meeting request to a potential mentor last week, but they haven't responded. Write a polite follow-up email to check in without being pushy.
images: A person looking at their phone, checking for messages.

questions.texte: Write a follow-up email. Include a polite reminder and an easy way for the recipient to respond.
questions.reponse: Example answer: 'Subject: Following Up: Meeting Request. Dear Dr. Smith, I hope this email finds you well. I'm writing to follow up on my previous email regarding a possible meeting to discuss career advice for software engineering. I understand you have a busy schedule, but I would greatly appreciate 15-20 minutes of your time if you are available. If the proposed time doesn't work, please feel free to suggest an alternative. Thank you for your consideration. Best regards, [Your Name]'

sousQuestions.texte: Analyze the effectiveness of the follow-up email. How does it balance persistence with politeness?
sousQuestions.reponse: The email is polite and respectful. It acknowledges the recipient's busy schedule ('I understand you have a busy schedule') and offers flexibility ('please feel free to suggest an alternative'). It reminds the recipient of the original request without being demanding. This approach increases the chances of a positive response.

enonce.texte: You need to schedule a meeting with the product owner, a senior designer, and two frontend developers to discuss the new mobile app design. The meeting must happen within the next 5 days. Write a meeting request email that includes a proposed agenda, time options, and a clear action item for attendees.
images: A calendar showing multiple time slots with different people's availability.

questions.texte: Write the meeting request email. Include all necessary components and make it easy for recipients to confirm their availability.
questions.reponse: Example answer: 'Subject: Meeting Request: Mobile App Design Review. Dear Team, I hope you're all having a productive week. I would like to schedule a 60-minute meeting to review and align on the mobile app design for our upcoming release. Proposed Agenda: 1. Review wireframes (10 min). 2. Discuss development feasibility (20 min). 3. Identify technical constraints (15 min). 4. Agree on next steps (15 min). I'm available on the following dates: - Tuesday at 10:00 AM - Wednesday at 2:00 PM - Thursday at 11:00 AM. Please reply with your availability or suggest an alternative time. Also, please come prepared with any questions or concerns about the design. Thank you. Best regards, [Your Name]'

sousQuestions.texte: Evaluate how the email facilitates scheduling. What makes it effective for a busy team?
sousQuestions.reponse: The email provides a clear agenda, which helps attendees prepare and ensures the meeting is productive. Offering multiple time options makes it easier for busy people to find a slot. The clear action item ('come prepared with any questions') ensures that attendees are engaged and the meeting is focused. The subject line is descriptive, making it easy to find in the inbox.
